text: NATIONAL SURVEY ARCHIVE
Plate 47: Coastal Triangulation, 1911 Resurvey

Digitised at 1200 dpi from the original vellum plate. The station coordinates below are transcribed from the field ledger and keep the
original Clarke 1880 figure, so users comparing against the modern network must apply the published datum shift before any computation.

Station BEACON HILL: 58 deg 12 min 41.30 sec N, 6 deg 22 min 08.71 sec W
Station CNOC ARD:    58 deg 11 min 57.02 sec N, 6 deg 19 min 44.55 sec W
Station SGEIR DUBH:  58 deg 13 min 22.87 sec N, 6 deg 17 min 30.12 sec W
Observer Notes

Heliograph signals from Beacon Hill were lost in haar on the morning rounds and all angles were repeated after noon. The theodolite,
Troughton and Simms No. 3, read to one second of arc, and each round of angles closed the horizon within three seconds before
acceptance.

Reduction follows Ordnance memorandum 44 of 1909. Spherical excess
distributed equally. Closing error of triangle 47-C: 1.88 seconds.

Conservation record: plate cleaned and rebacked March 1961; fungal foxing at NE corner
stabilised. Access copy ASA-47-1911-R2. Original held in vault 9, humidity class B.
Baseline Measurements

The Loch Roag base of 1909 was remeasured with invar tapes
numbers 61 and 63 under 15 pounds tension. Twelve bays gave
a mean of 3,662.114 metres with a spread of 4.1 millimetres.

Tape 61 standardisation: 30.000,42 m at 14.2 C, coefficient 0.0000006
Tape 63 standardisation: 30.000,38 m at 14.2 C, coefficient 0.0000007
Field temperatures by mercury thermometers 118 and 121, read to 0.2 C
Adjustment Summary

Least squares adjustment over 31 conditions closed the network
with a maximum residual of 0.94 seconds on line 47-52. Side
lengths are tabulated on plate 48 with their logarithms.

Archivist note: the 1911 party lists J. Macleod as observer and A. Ross as recorder.
Wages ledger cross-reference WL-1911-224. Photograph album PA-19 shows camp at Cnoc Ard.

Digitisation metadata: scanner SG-1200-IV, target IT8.7/2 batch 2026-03, delta E mean 1.1.
File checksum sha256 9c41...e7 recorded in accession register AR-2026-118. Scanned by K.O.

Comparison with the 1852 Primary Triangulation
Where the 1911 stations reoccupy primary marks, coordinate shifts stay below 0.4 metres except at Sgeir Dubh, where the cairn had been
rebuilt seaward of the original centre mark. A buried bottle holding the 1852 centre punch was recovered at half a metre and the new
pillar was set over it directly, restoring continuity of the mark.

Gravity and Deflection Observations
Pendulum gravity at Beacon Hill agrees with the Bouguer prediction within 11 milligals. Astronomical latitude shows a deflection of the
vertical of 4.2 seconds south, ascribed to the mass of the gneiss ridge east of the station, and the azimuth condition was therefore
carried on Cnoc Ard instead.

Availability and Citation
High resolution scans of plates 44 through 52 are available on reader request under licence NLA-OG-4. Cite this plate as National
Survey Archive, Coastal Triangulation Resurvey of 1911, plate 47, accession AR-2026-118, digitised 2026. Derived vector data carries
the same licence and must reproduce this citation in full.

Related Holdings
The archive holds the computation books for divisions 44 to 52, the observer's diary for the 1911 season, and glass negatives of the
station cairns. Requests for the diary require a conservation review because the binding is friable along the spine.

Reader services: the search room opens Tuesday to Saturday, 09:30 to 16:45, with document ordering closing at 15:30. Photography is
permitted without flash under permit PH-11, and bulk imaging requests route through the digitisation programme office.

GEOTHERMAL TEST WELL KV-9
Quarterly Integrity Report, Q3 2026

1. Summary of Operations
The wellhead held a stable 41.3 bar across the quarter. Flow
testing on 12 August reached 96 kg/s at 243 degrees Celsius,
matching the drawdown model within 2.1 percent.

2. Casing Inspection
Ultrasonic logs show wall thickness above 11.2 mm everywhere
except joint 41, where pitting reduced it to 9.7 mm. The joint
remains inside the 8.5 mm retirement threshold.

3. Instrumentation
Downhole gauge DG-118 drifted 0.4 bar and was recalibrated.
Fibre line FL-2 returned clean DTS traces after splice repair.
Appendix A: Sample Assays

Sample KV9-S31: silica 612 mg/kg, chloride 88 mg/kg, pH 7.9
Sample KV9-S32: silica 598 mg/kg, chloride 91 mg/kg, pH 8.0
Sample KV9-S33: silica 640 mg/kg, chloride 84 mg/kg, pH 7.8

Note 1: Assay uncertainty is 3 percent
relative, one sigma, per lab method
LM-410 revision D.

Note 2: Chloride trend remains below
the scaling advisory limit defined in
operations memo OM-2214.

4. Reinjection Performance
Injection well KV-9R accepted the full 71 kg/s return stream at
18.9 bar wellhead pressure. Tracer test T-14 shows 4.1 percent
breakthrough after 62 days, unchanged from the spring campaign.

5. Planned Work
A caliper rerun of joints 38 through 44 is scheduled for early
November, together with replacement of the annulus bleed valve
and a full recalibration of the fiscal metering skid.
Appendix B: Vibration Survey

Pump P-201: 2.1 mm/s RMS at bearing housing, within ISO zone B
Pump P-202: 4.8 mm/s RMS, rising trend, realignment scheduled
Separator feed line: no cavitation signature above 2 kilohertz

6. Environmental Compliance
Hydrogen sulphide at the site boundary averaged 3.1 micrograms
per cubic metre, well under the 15 microgram consent ceiling.
Brine pond levels stayed within the freeboard requirement and
no discharge events were recorded during the quarter.
Report KV9-Q3-2026-INT, revision 2. Approved by R. Steinsdottir, 30 September 2026.
THE MERIDIAN LEDGER
Founded 1908. Weekend Edition, 14 November 2026.

Tidal Array Delivers First Power to Grid
The Stormness tidal array fed 18 megawatts into the northern grid on Thursday, three weeks ahead of
schedule. Engineers credit the redesigned blade pitch controller, which survived the spring tides that
destroyed the 2023 prototype field, and a subsea hub that lets divers isolate one turbine without
darkening the whole string.

Turbine seven remains offline after a seal failure flooded its nacelle in October. Divers recovered the
unit intact and the operator expects a rebuilt gearbox to spin by January, with the insurance survey
already closed out and spares landed at the quayside store.
Shipping Notices

MV Kittiwake, berth 4, discharging aggregate until Tuesday.
MV Solan Goose, berth 9, loading 2,400 t of cured timber.
Pilot boarding moves to the eastern anchorage from 06:00.

Tide table, Stormness Sound: high 04:41 and 17:02, low 10:48 and 23:11.
Heights 3.4 m and 3.1 m. Springs return on the 21st. Chart datum LAT.
Notice 2026-118: racon on the Skerry buoy unreliable until further notice.

Classified index: employment 12, marine sales 14, legal notices 15, tenders 17.
Printed at Quayside Works on 45 gsm newsprint. ISSN 0140-7723. Price two pounds.
Council Approves Breakwater Levy

A harbour levy of 40 pence per landed tonne passed by nine votes to three on Wednesday night. Proceeds
are ring-fenced for the eastern breakwater rebuild, estimated at 6.2 million pounds over four seasons of
work, and the first caisson contract goes to tender in February.

Fisheries representatives abstained, calling instead for a berthing rebate for vessels under twelve
metres. The council agreed to review the rebate at the March sitting once a season of levy receipts can
be set against the dredging account.
Weather and Sea State

Saturday: southwest gale eight, easing six by evening. Rain.
Sunday: west five, showers, good visibility between squalls.
Sea area Fair Isle: rough becoming moderate. Icing nil.

Corrections: last week's edition gave the Kittiwake's tonnage as 4,100; the correct
figure is 4,010 gross tonnes. The Ledger regrets the error. Contact corrections@ledger.

Ferry Timetable Consultation Opens
The winter timetable consultation runs until 5 December. Proposals cut the Tuesday freight-only sailing
and add a late Friday passenger run. Responses go to the transport partnership office or any harbour
master's post box before the closing date.

School Boat Prize Returns to Northside
Northside Secondary took the inter-school sailing trophy for the third year, finishing four points clear
over the combined southern crews in a shifting easterly breeze that favoured the lighter boats.

SITE PLAN SP-04: QUAYSIDE ENERGY CENTRE
Scale 1:200 at A0. Grid: local datum QEC-2026. Sheet 4 of 12.

GENERAL NOTES
1. All dimensions are in millimetres unless noted. Verify every setting-out dimension on site
against the QEC-2026 grid monuments before excavation. Report discrepancies over 15 mm to the
engineer before proceeding with the affected work.

2. Underground HV cable route 11kV-R2 crosses the northern access at chainage 48.20. Hand dig
within 1500 mm of the marked route. Cable cover tiles must be reinstated with warning tape at
300 mm above the duct crown.

3. Drainage runs DR-7 to DR-11 fall at 1:150 toward manhole MH-19. Invert levels are tabulated
on sheet SP-09. Flexible couplings within 600 mm of every structure face, both sides.

4. The attenuation tank base slab is cast on 50 mm blinding over compacted type 1 fill at 95
percent modified proctor. Waterstop at every construction joint; the kicker pour includes the
north wall starter bars.

EARTHWORKS
Strip topsoil to 300 mm and stockpile on the western bund at a maximum height of 2.5 metres.

Excavations deeper than 1200 mm require trench support to the temporary works designer's
details. Groundwater strike below 4.1 metres was recorded in borehole BH-06; allow for sump
pumping in the tank excavation.

Perimeter fence type F2: 2.4 metre paladin mesh on 60 x 60 SHS posts at 3.0 metre centres, set

Acoustic barrier along gridline 2 from chainage 0 to 64: 3.6 metre absorptive panels, minimum

NIGHTSIDE OPERATIONS MANUAL
Section 7: Thermal Watch Procedures

During eclipse passes the radiator loop runs unpumped and the watch
officer logs the plateau temperature of both accumulator tanks every
eleven minutes. A divergence beyond four kelvin between the tanks
indicates a stuck bypass valve and the recovery checklist on page
ninety-one applies without further authorization.

Heater bank C remains isolated while the survey instrument records. Its
inrush transient couples into the magnetometer boom and has produced false
substorm signatures twice this quarter, most recently on the descending
node over the Weddell Sea anomaly.

Watch handover requires three items:
1. Signed plateau log with divergence column initialed
2. Valve position table read back against telemetry
3. Heater bank C isolation breaker photographed

Deviations are recorded in the anomaly ledger before end of shift. The
ledger is the controlling document in any disagreement between console
notes and downlinked housekeeping frames.
